title: House Robber
statement: Houses along a street each hold some amount of money, given by the array nums. You can't take from two adjacent houses on the same night. Return the maximum amount of money you can collect.
edgeCases: skipping two in a row is optimal: [2,1,1,2]
keyInsights: At each house, either skip it (best up to i-1) or take it (nums[i] + best up to i-2)
Greedy 'take every other house' fails, e.g. [2,1,1,2]
hintLadder: Try your approach on nums = [2,1,1,2]. Does taking every other house give the best answer?
At house i you have two choices: take it or skip it. What does each choice mean for house i-1?
best(i) = max(best(i-1), nums[i] + best(i-2)). Iterate once, keeping only the last two values.
